claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with a few questions:

**First, how many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my child - I have one child that I'd like to check eligibility for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! So you're inquiring about one child. That's helpful.

**What is your child's name?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Now I have a few questions to assess eligibility for Alex.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Before I proceed, let me check the specific eligibility criteria to ensure I ask you all the right questions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! I've reviewed the eligibility criteria. Now I have some more questions for you to determine if you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means either you live with them (which you've confirmed) or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them - such as on food, clothes, or pocket money.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex - they live with me and I take care of all their needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to check a few more things to confirm your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that you're fostering Alex. That's important information.

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. I have one more question to complete my assessment.

**Are you a British citizen or do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a Crown servant?)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the rules based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old (under 16, so eligible age)
- You live in the UK with Alex
- You are responsible for Alex and care for all their needs
- You are fostering Alex
- The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance
- You are a British citizen

Based on the eligibility criteria I've reviewed, you should qualify for Child Benefit for Alex. According to the rules, you can get Child Benefit if you foster a child, as long as the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance – which is your situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Congratulations!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. You meet all the necessary criteria:

✓ Alex is under 16 years old
✓ You live in the UK with Alex
✓ You are responsible for Alex's care
✓ You are fostering Alex and the local council is not paying towards their accommodation or maintenance
✓ You have the right to reside in the UK as a British citizen

You should now be able to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any further questions or if your circumstances change, feel free to contact HMRC or the Child Benefit Office for assistance.
